aggregate_over_runs.zero_item_reason: Both rooms’ catalogues are keyed to synthetic entities that have no approved offer on file, so every candidate was labelled unsupported rather than shown as a live pick. Qloo returned rows; the app refused to present them as offerable. Not counted as a failure, and not hidden.

gate.requirement: 3 cities, >=10 distinct artists, >=5 after the popularity band, non-empty explainability
gate.note: Chicago, Austin and Nashville each returned 20 artists with the location signal, 20 after the popularity band, and a non-empty English description on every entity. Venues is therefore the lead pack; retail ships as the proof that a pack is configuration, not code.

rows.name: Excluding entities and tags at query time
Popularity band as an API filter

field_notes: No affinity or score field is returned by /v2/insights for entity results (checked on every row of every verified call). Qloo's contribution is the ORDER plus the popularity, obscurity and audience attributes. Taste Brain therefore shows Qloo's rank as the authoritative signal and labels its 0..1 fit value as derived from that rank.
Tags arrive as objects {id, name, type}, not plain strings. Rules match on the tag id.
short_descriptions is a list of {lang, text}; the English entry is used and the rest ignored.

ablation_arms.reading: Arm A is the ranking the proposal shipped, so it is 1.0 by definition — the informative arms are B, C, D and E. Ordering without Qloo at all lands at or below τ 0.15 and moves every top-k position; destroying Qloo’s order with a fixed seed gives τ ≈ 0.09 and overlap ≈ chance (0.4 expected at k=10 of 25). So the shipped order carries Qloo’s signal and nothing else in the pipeline manufactures one. Where the two signals bite differs by pack and is reported as measured, not asserted: in venues, removing either the room or the seeds replaces all 10 top positions; in retail and restaurants the no-location arm returned the identical order (τ 1, overlap 1), so the app publishes local_lift 0 on every item rather than implying the city moved anything.

rubric.source: qloo.devpost.com/rules — four criteria, equally weighted. These are self-scores written from the measured evidence above, not judges’ scores.

criteria.name: Technological Implementation
criteria.why: 37 real reads across 6 distinct workflows, 8 live proposals through one engine with 3 config-only packs, 10 capabilities verified against the API and 3 honestly recorded as accepted-but-empty.
criteria.gap: Restraint costs demo volume: 2 of 7 rooms return 0 items because their synthetic catalogues have no approved offer, which is the correct answer and a weaker screen.

criteria.name: Design
criteria.why: Twelve screens reachable from one nav; every result carries its provenance — the header badge, the measured mode mix ("154 of 154 steps read from Qloo on this run"), evidence cards with Qloo’s own figures, and a ledger whose hashes are recomputed on view.
criteria.gap: No deployment, so nothing beyond localhost has been seen by another human; screenshots are the only shareable artefact.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
criteria.why: The buying/menuing/booking decision is stated as a business problem with a named approver, and the guardrails match it: approval requires a human, no rule is silently bypassed, and every rejection has a flip point telling the operator which threshold would have changed the answer.
criteria.gap: No business outcome is measured or claimed. 8 proposals from one operator on one day is a demonstration, not evidence of revenue impact.

criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
criteria.why: The non-obvious move is treating the API as the thing to be proven rather than the thing to be praised: ablation arms D/E show Qloo’s order surviving while its shuffled control collapses to chance, and the pipeline will downgrade its own LIVE badge when a run actually read nothing.
criteria.gap: Taste Lift cannot publish an LLM comparison on this host — no LLM key, so arm A never ran and no lift figure is fabricated.

repeat_live_run.meaning: Asked live again minutes later: every answer was already in .private-cache, so the run made no live read and the badge followed the bytes.

defect_found_and_fixed.finding: The reason a live request came back Cached lived only on the request session. Once stored, the proposal said mode: cached and nothing else, so a viewer could not tell a quota degrade from an all-cached answer.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: Proposal.degrade_reason is written with the run (server/src/types.ts, agents/pipeline.ts) and shown on the Plan screen; Finals Mode re-serve states its own reason.
defect_found_and_fixed.verified: Browser at localhost:3000 — note rendered above the audience portrait, header badge CACHED with 0/130 fetched now. tsc --noEmit clean on server and client; vitest 84/84; 0 live reads spent on this check.

known_gaps: Nothing is pushed: the public repo, license visibility and demo URL the rules require are outstanding.
restaurants/loc_westside and venues/venue_redroom return 0 live items for the reason stated above.
venue runs mark items needs_data + approval_blocked until the operator supplies offer terms.
The harness day counter is in-memory and resets on dev-server reload; the saved call log is the durable spend record.

Retail and restaurant runs show local_lift 0 on every item: for those seeds the live no-location arm returned the identical order, so the "local taste" story is a venues story and the UI does not pretend otherwise.

Replay ships synthetic fixtures for 5 of the 7 rooms (venue_redroom, store_1..3, loc_westside); the two rooms configured to draw on live Qloo (Corner Hall, Alder Room) have none, because committed fixtures may not contain live Qloo payloads and their tracked room/seed names are fictional. Offline they now return an honest empty run that names the missing fixture file.
Taste Lift arm A did not run (no LLM key on this host), so no LLM-vs-grounded lift figure exists.
